text: Cataphasia (or Kata- ) [Gr. katafasiV , assent]: Ger. Kataphasie ; Fr. cataphasie ( acataphasie ); Ital. catafasia . A degeneration of speech, usually connected with serious nervous disease, in which the patient, either spontaneously or in answer to questions, constantly repeats the same word or phrases. The word is also used (Kussmaul) to describe serious degeneration in the formation of sentences, the patient's language being reduced, like that of a child just beginning to speak, to the skeleton words of a sentence with little grammatical construction (hence also termed agrammatism) and much repetition. See SPEECH AND ITS DEFECTS. ( J.J. )
